complexity.notes: Behaviorally correct, but two flaws. First, a memory leak: on eviction the key is removed from `stored` yet left in `self.cache`, so the dict never shrinks — it stays correct only because `get` gates the returned value on `stored` membership; the eviction branch should also delete the key from the dict. Second, `get` tests `key in self.stored` twice; evaluating it once and reusing the result would be tidier. The stated O(1)-per-operation requirement is not met: O(1) average per operation is achievable with ||a hashmap whose values point into a doubly linked list, or simply collections.OrderedDict with move_to_end and popitem(last=False)||.
complexity.space: O(distinct keys ever inserted) — evicted keys are deleted from the list but never from the dict, so it grows unboundedly; the recency list itself is O(capacity)
complexity.summary: Stores values in a dict and tracks recency in a plain list, moving touched keys to the tail and dropping the head on overflow. Membership tests, remove(), and del list[0] are all linear in the capacity, so each operation costs O(capacity) rather than O(1).
complexity.time_average: O(capacity) per get/put; the dict operations are O(1) average but every operation pays a linear scan, remove, or front-deletion on the recency list
complexity.time_worst: O(capacity) per get/put; adversarial int-hash collisions in the dict cannot exceed the already-linear list operations
